title: Dot Blots Analysis in the Separation of Anti-HIV Antibodies
author: Angel A Justiz-Vaillant
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.bjm4kk8w
materials: Finally, 5 μL of the substrate 3,3’,5,5’-tetramethylbenzidine (Sigma Chemical Co., St Louis, MO, USA) is added and the mixture is incubated for 20 min.
The membrane is left to dry.

steps.title: Spot diluted sample on membrane
steps.instruction: Apply two (2) µL of a 1:2 dilution of chicken IgY or two (2) µL of rat or cat serum onto the nitrocellulose paper.

steps.title: Load membrane into BioDot apparatus
steps.instruction: Place the nitrocellulose membrane into a BioDot SF apparatus (Bio‑Rad Laboratories, Richmond, CA, USA).

steps.title: Block membrane with serum buffer
steps.instruction: Block the membrane by adding 5 µL per well of fetal bovine serum prepared in 1 % Tris‑buffered saline.

steps.title: Add peroxidase‑labeled HIV conjugate
steps.instruction: Add 5 µL of a commercial peroxidase‑labeled HIV protein conjugate (Murex Diagnostics, Norcross, USA) to each well and allow it to drain by gravity.

steps.title: Wash to stop reaction
steps.instruction: Stop the reaction by washing the wells with distilled water under vacuum.
